column18: THE MODEL, not the post-processing. All three columns decay to the SAME degree from wk<=2 to wk>=9: psi 55%, pred_smooth 61%, pred_raw 65% of their early level, while observed holds at 95%. In-sample (last 26 wk before each cutoff) the model is well calibrated -- psi 0.273 / pred_raw 0.226 vs observed 0.238 -- and out-of-sample at wk>=9 psi is 0.089 against observed 0.214, i.e. 42% of the truth. This is a systematic horizon-growing LEVEL COLLAPSE of about -0.125, and it is the largest single defect measured anywhere in this programme. It explains: psi losing to persistence (whose bias is ~+0.02), psi losing to a flat climatology, wave 17's finding that psi only beats a constant where the target is FLAT, and DS-02 (calibration driving psi_star_b to its floor because psi arrives too low and too dead). column6: audit what country-variability capacity the production architecture actually has
column17: (1) Country/region conditioning acts ONLY on the trunk's 32-dim OUTPUT -- z_r=(1+g_r)z+b_r then z_c=(1+g_c)z_r+b_c -- while the LSTM weights that process the 13-week sequence are IDENTICAL for all 40 countries. So no country can have a different lag structure, response timing or persistence, yet measured decay ratios span 0.083 (ZWE) to 1.387 (MWI), a 17x spread in exactly the property the architecture forces to be common. lstm_film_suitability.R's own header records that the input-FiLM and hypernet branches were DROPPED in the gauge_A-only port -- input-FiLM is the missing capability and has prior art in the sandbox. (2) tanh gamma gives (1+gamma) in (0,2), so country modulation is SIGN-PRESERVING: a country can damp or double a trunk feature but never reverse it. (3) ZERO static country covariates in the 38-feature v7.3 set, while 17 sit UNUSED in the 298-column panel (Piped_Water, Open_Defecation, Unimproved_Sanitation, Surface_Water, population_density, urban_population_pct, GDP, poverty_ratio, ...). Country identity is therefore a bare learned ID embedding (dim 16), so the model can pool only by hard region membership, never by similarity -- most data-hungry exactly where data is scarcest (RWA 29 nonzero weeks, KEN 41, AGO 51). (4) country_balance = FALSE: the loss is unbalanced across countries, so the shared trunk is fitted in proportion to data volume and learns the high-burden snf_2 response, which PREDICTS the measured asymmetry. The flag already exists in .psi_configure_loss() and appears never to have been tested. (5) partial_pool_lambda is ONE global scalar (0.1): shrinkage is not information-weighted, so RWA (29 weeks) is shrunk exactly as hard as NGA (206). Also: predictive intervals are seed dispersion, so they are not country-specific at all -- a data-poor country does not get wider intervals, which is backwards and is why WIS punishes unevenly (RWA -2.78).

IDENTITY AT INIT, verified: the FiLM generator's embedding is zero-initialised and Keras defaults bias_initializer to zeros, so gamma_in = tanh(0) = 0 and beta_in = 0 and (1+0)*X+0 = X exactly -- the arm starts AT the production model. Measured init deviation 1.5e-02 sits INSIDE the seed-to-seed init spread (1.1e-02 to 6.1e-02), i.e. it is RNG-stream displacement from the extra layers, not a forward-pass difference. Only the embedding is zeroed, never the dense: zeroing both makes the branch permanently dead (zero input gives a zero weight gradient, zero weight gives a zero embedding gradient).

column6: audit the 12 static country covariates in the panel for D9 viability
column17: All 12 are CLEAN: 0% NA, all 16 pool countries present. But 8 of them (Piped_Water, Other_Improved_Water, Unimproved_Water, Surface_Water, Septic_or_Sewer_Sanitation, Other_Improved_Sanitation, Unimproved_Sanitation, Open_Defecation) are EXACTLY CONSTANT IN TIME (per-country temporal CV = 0.000) while varying strongly across countries (cross-country CV 0.44-1.18). The other 4 are only slowly time-varying (population_density 0.23, urban_population_pct 0.10, GDP 0.50, poverty_ratio 0.18) and are effectively constant within a 13-week window too. CONSEQUENCE FOR D9's DESIGN: appending them to the 38 SEQUENCE features (the naive reading, call it D9a) would feed the LSTM a constant channel, which it can only use as a per-country bias -- and the country FiLM's beta_c already supplies exactly that, so D9a is close to a no-op by construction. The right form is D9b: feed them into the FiLM GENERATOR in place of (or alongside) the bare country-ID embedding, so a country's modulation becomes a FUNCTION OF ITS CHARACTERISTICS. Then a data-poor country (RWA 29 nonzero weeks, KEN 41, AGO 51) inherits modulation from characteristically similar countries instead of learning a private 16-dim embedding from almost no data -- which is the actual fix for 'the model pools only by hard region membership, never by similarity'. D9b also composes with N5: same generator, different conditioning input.

column6: how to build static-covariate FiLM conditioning WITHOUT a new model input
column17: The obvious build adds a new model input (X_static through the bundle, the sequence builder, both slicers and make_x) -- 5+ touch points on paths that every existing arm depends on. Touch points: ONE (encoders gains a `country_static` field at build_suitability_sequences.R:355, and encoders already flows everywhere the model needs it). Two variants fall out for free: trainable = FALSE forces country differences to be a LINEAR MAP of WASH/density/urban/GDP with zero free parameters per country (maximal shrinkage, the strongest test of 'pool by similarity'), and trainable = TRUE is the same thing as a warm start. column6: test the wave-22 regional split against a PURE FIT-NOISE null (P000R vs P000, same spec)
column17: THE SPLIT IS NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE REGIONAL STRUCTURE OF FIT NOISE. Fitting delta ~ incumbent_skill + I(region==snf_1) on 16 countries: C9d (class C, post-processing) region adds p = 0.0804, R2 0.374; P000-vs-P001 (class R, data/features) p = 0.1173, R2 0.192; and P000R-vs-P000 -- THE SAME SPEC, so the delta is PURE SEED NOISE -- p = 0.1416, R2 0.181. The sign pattern did replicate across two arms (snf_1 all non-positive twice) but so does the noise, and I reported the p = 0.045 without ever asking what the null looked like. WHAT SURVIVES: the architecture audit's findings are STRUCTURAL FACTS about the model, independent of any delta analysis -- conditioning acts on the trunk output rather than the dynamics, country_balance is FALSE, there are no static country covariates, and tanh gamma is sign-preserving. N8/N5/N6/D9b remain well-motivated as structural fixes; what is gone is the claim that the arm deltas SHOW the model failing regionally. ONLY THE REPLICATE MADE THIS TESTABLE: without P000R there was no null to compare against and the regional story would have stood.

column6: what would the floor be under alternative aggregations, applied identically to the P000/P000R replicate pair
column16: ESCALATE: RESOLUTION IS AN ESTIMAND CHOICE, NOT A COMPUTE LIMIT
column17: ONE COUNTRY CARRIES 87% OF THE FLOOR. Leave-one-country-out on the current estimand: dropping COD takes the floor from 0.0912 to 0.0120 (13% of full); every other country changes it by <=10% (SOM 90%, SSD 98%, BDI 98%, TZA 99%). ALTERNATIVE AGGREGATIONS, each applied identically to the same replicate pair, with floor/|S| as the scale-normalised resolution (lower is better): CURRENT median-over-blocks + sqrt-burden floor 0.0912, |S| 0.32, ratio 0.285 -- THE WORST OF THE SIX. mean-over-blocks 0.0861 / 0.453 = 0.190. Equal country weights 0.0598 / 0.368 = 0.163. Winsorise per-country skill at +/-1: 0.0504 / 0.236 = 0.214. Winsorise at +/-0.5: 0.0143 / 0.125 = 0.114, i.e. 2.5x better signal-to-noise. Equal + winsorise +/-1: 0.0312 / 0.173 = 0.180. CRUCIALLY the floor falls FASTER than the scale compresses (winsorising at +/-0.5 cuts the floor 6.4x while shrinking |S| only 2.3x), so this is a genuine resolution gain and not just a rescaling. MECHANISM: WIS-skill = 1 - WIS_m/WIS_b is UNBOUNDED BELOW -- a country-block 4x worse than baseline scores -3 (RWA reaches -2.8) -- and those extreme cells are exactly where fit noise is amplified, so the unbounded lower tail is what destroys the objective's resolution. THE TRADE, stated honestly: winsorising caps how much a catastrophic country can matter, and psi's failure mode IS catastrophic in some countries, so it buys resolution by giving up sensitivity to disaster. +/-1 is the defensible middle (floor 0.0504). NOTE mean-over-blocks is BOTH more resolvable than median AND fixes the non-additivity that caused the wave-17 retraction, at a smaller conceptual cost than winsorising. ALL OF THESE ARE OBJECTIVE CHANGES (PROTOCOL 5.1) AND THEREFORE THE USER'S DECISION, NOT MINE.

column6: objective v4 candidate: mean-over-blocks + sqrt-burden + a ONE-SIDED floor at -2
column17: SUPERSEDES the symmetric-winsor options in FLOOR-ESTIMAND, which were MISSPECIFIED. Skill = 1 - WIS_m/WIS_b is BOUNDED ABOVE by 1 (max observed 0.90 over 360 cells) and UNBOUNDED BELOW (min -12.20, q05 -3.04), so a symmetric cap either never binds on the upper side (+/-1, +/-2) or destroys real successes (+/-0.5 caps 61.1% of cells including 18.6% from ABOVE -- degenerate, and its 0.0143 floor is an artifact of discarding the scale, not a resolution gain). The correct bound is ONE-SIDED. Measured on the P000/P000R replicate pair, floor and floor/|S| (lower better), with the share of cells the bound touches: CURRENT median+sqrt 0.0912 / 0.284 / 0.0%; median+sqrt floor -2 0.0908 / 0.293 / 6.7% (the median is insensitive to tail depth, so bounding it buys nothing); mean+sqrt 0.0861 / 0.190 / 0.0%; **mean+sqrt floor -2 0.0361 / 0.091 / 6.7%**; mean+sqrt floor -1 0.0060 / 0.023 / 21.7%; mean+equal floor -1 0.0013 / 0.006 / 21.7%. RECOMMENDATION: mean-over-blocks + sqrt-burden + one-sided floor at -2. It gives a 3.1x resolution gain (0.284 -> 0.091), touches only 6.7% of cells and all of them in the catastrophic tail, PRESERVES the burden weighting that is the objective's stated intent, and mean-over-blocks independently fixes the median-then-weight non-additivity behind the wave-17 retraction. Going to -1 buys more resolution but caps 21.7%; going to equal weights abandons the burden intent. CONSEQUENCE IF ADOPTED: every score in the ledger must be recomputed, but that is FREE (scoring only, caches exist). NOT ENACTED.

column6: C9d's delta under each candidate estimand
column17: C9d, which I have repeatedly called the largest effect in the ledger (+0.1411), REVERSES to -0.1051 under mean-over-blocks, and the reversal is readable (|-0.105| > that estimand's floor of 0.086). This is a second, independent reason to prefer mean-over-blocks: it is sensitive to exactly the failure mode the objective should punish, and the median hid it.

column17: USER REDIRECTED THE PROGRAMME ONTO PLAIN ACCURACY AND WAS RIGHT. Replicate noise across two fits of the SAME model (P000 vs P000R), as a share of the metric's level: MAE 0.09%, R2 0.29%, WIS 0.41%, RMSE 0.60% -- against WIS-SKILL 28.41%. The skill ratio is ~300x noisier than MAE because it divides by a per-country baseline WIS that itself varies and is unbounded below. EVERYTHING the last several waves spent on the 'floor' (0.0912), T7 resolution failure, and the estimand proposal was chasing an artifact of that ratio: on MAE a 2% improvement is trivially detectable. The floor work was not worthless -- it correctly killed the +0.105 v7.3-vs-v7.4 claim and the regional split -- but it became the main event when the question was accuracy.

column6: horizon-dependent blend weight: lambda_country (from C10) x a POOLED horizon shape, both from earlier cutoffs' realised blocks
column7: persistence is anchored on the last observation so its edge should be largest at week 1 and decay with lead, while psi's climate signal does not decay the same way -- so a horizon-constant lambda must be leaving value on the table
column16: BEST OOS ACCURACY IN THE PROGRAMME
column17: MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY THE FITTED CURVE. Pooled optimal weight on psi by horizon week: wk1-2 0.05, wk3-4 0.15, wk5-6 0.40, wk7-8 0.20-0.25, wk9-10 0.25-0.30, wk11-12 0.35-0.50, wk13 0.40. Near-pure persistence at short lead, psi earning up to half the weight by week 11-12 -- exactly the predicted shape. ACCURACY on N8's psi: C12c_C11h MAE 0.1570 (-27.9% vs production 0.2229), R2_corr 0.233, R2_sse -0.289, WIS 0.1434 -- all three the best measured anywhere in this programme. Only 5.4% worse than persistence (0.1490), down from 49.6% for production psi. The MULTIPLICATIVE form matters: C12b (horizon shape alone, pooled across countries) is 0.1679 and C12c alone is 0.1718, while C12c_C11h combining the per-country level, the pooled horizon shape and the level anchor is 0.1570. C7c's failure (pooled horizon curve with climatology, -0.874 on the old metric) was about pooling REPLACING the country term, not about horizon dependence itself.

column6: MAE by horizon band for the leading blend vs persistence, with LEAKAGE-CLEAN lambda
column16: MY FIRST NUMBER WAS LEAKY; THE REAL WIN IS +1.7%
column17: I first computed this with the lambda curve HARDCODED from the last cutoff's fit and applied to every block, which leaks the curve into the early blocks. That version said the blend beat persistence at weeks 9-13 by +8.0%. Recomputed inside the leakage-clean pipeline (lambda estimated per cutoff from EARLIER cutoffs only): weeks 1-4 blend 0.1032 vs persistence 0.0983 (-5.0%); weeks 5-8 0.1347 vs 0.1239 (-8.7%); weeks 9-13 0.1729 vs 0.1758 (+1.7%). So the blend DOES beat persistence at the 12-week end, but by 1.7% and not 8% -- the hardcoded curve inflated it about fivefold. Caught by re-deriving it inside the pipeline instead of trusting the hand-held script. THE LOSSES AT WEEKS 1-8 DIAGNOSE A DEFECT: lambda initialised to 1 (pure psi) when there is no history to estimate it, so the first cutoff ran as RAW PSI, the weakest forecast on the board. Absent evidence that psi helps, the safe prior is the STRONG baseline. Fixed to default lambda = 0 (pure persistence) in C10/C7b/C12b/C12c; re-measuring.

column6: default lambda when no history exists to estimate it: 1 (pure psi) -> 0 (pure persistence)
column7: the first cutoff has no earlier blocks, so it was running as RAW PSI -- the weakest forecast on the board -- purely because of an initialisation choice
column16: BEST RESULT: BEATS PERSISTENCE AT 12 WEEKS BY 5.7%
column17: ONE-LINE CHANGE, LARGE EFFECT. MAE by horizon band, leakage-clean, before -> after the prior fix: weeks 1-4 -5.0% -> -3.1%; weeks 5-8 -8.7% -> -0.5%; WEEKS 9-13 +1.7% -> +5.7% vs persistence. Overall burden-weighted MAE 0.1570 -> 0.1511 (-30.6% vs production psi 0.2229), against persistence 0.1490 -- so only 1.4% worse OVERALL, and that deficit is entirely weeks 1-4 where the last observation is near-optimal by construction and the blend correctly defers to it. R2_corr 0.260 and R2_sse -0.197 and WIS 0.1413 are all the best measured in this programme (production: 0.098 / -1.249 / 0.1860). THE HEADLINE, stated carefully: at the 12-WEEK horizon this beats BOTH production psi (0.2186 raw at weeks 9-13) and persistence (0.1758) -- 0.1658, i.e. 24% better than production and 5.7% better than persistence. NOTE C12b (horizon shape only, pooled, no per-country term) is 0.1530, nearly matching C12c_C11h's 0.1511, so once the horizon shape and the prior are right the per-country term adds little -- worth remembering before spending anything on refining it.

column6: replace the flat-persistence anchor with a damped trend: anchor(w) = level + slope * sum(phi^k), phi from {0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9} chosen per cutoff on EARLIER cutoffs only
column7: the anchor carries 60-95% of the blend's weight, so improving IT raises the whole product rather than just the psi side; flat persistence cannot extrapolate a rising or falling epidemic at all
column17: SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: phi = 0 reduces EXACTLY to flat persistence, so the arm can only lose through estimation error in phi, not through the form. Slope is an OLS fit on the last 8 observed weeks at or before the cutoff; phi is chosen pooled across countries (one scalar per cutoff -- a per-country phi would be ~1 block per cell, the density that killed C7c). SELECTED PHI per cutoff: 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0, 0, 0.5 -- damping chosen in 4 of 9, flat in the rest, so the estimator is discriminating rather than always reaching for the trend.

column6: damped-trend anchor instead of flat persistence
column7: improving the anchor raises the whole blend since it carries 60-95% of the weight
column17: A2 alone MAE 0.1524 vs flat persistence 0.1490, and A2_C12c 0.1531 vs C12c_C11h 0.1511 -- WORSE on both. WIS is much worse (0.1707 vs 0.1413), which is the tell: extrapolating a slope widens the error distribution. R2_sse is marginally better (-0.188 vs -0.197) and R2_corr 0.239, so the trend does carry a little scale information, but not enough to pay for the variance it adds. MECHANISM: phi = 0.5 was selected in 4 of 9 cutoffs on earlier-cutoff MAE and did not generalise to the held-out block -- the same thin-history selection failure as C7's lambda -> 1.00 and B-CAL2's per-country choice. THE RECENT 8-WEEK SLOPE DOES NOT CARRY USABLE SIGNAL AT 9-13 WEEK LEADS. This closes the 'better anchor' avenue: flat persistence is the right anchor, and the remaining levers are the lambda curve's shape and the psi input itself.

column6: impose monotonicity on the lambda horizon curve by isotonic regression (theory says the weight on psi must RISE with lead)
column7: the fitted curve dips non-monotonically (0.40 at wk5-6 down to 0.20 at wk7) on ~90 cells per horizon week, so the dips should be noise and constraining them should help
column16: A WASH -- AND THAT CLOSES THE BLEND FAMILY
column17: MAE 0.1508 vs C12c_C11h 0.1511: an improvement of 0.0003, about 0.2%, against MAE replicate noise of 0.09%. Technically ~2x noise, practically a wash; WIS 0.1411 vs 0.1413 is identical and R2_corr is marginally WORSE (0.257 vs 0.260). So the non-monotone dips were not costing anything -- the blend is insensitive to lambda's fine structure. TAKEN WITH C12b (pooled horizon shape, NO per-country term, 0.1530) AND A2 (better anchor, REJECTED), THE BLEND MACHINERY IS SATURATED: the anchor is right, the horizon shape is right, the per-country term adds little, and smoothing the curve adds nothing. REMAINING GAINS MUST COME FROM A BETTER PSI -- the F fold ladder, D9b, N6 -- not from more post-processing. That is a useful negative: it stops the programme grinding on free-but-exhausted levers and points all remaining compute at the psi input.

column17: Commits 0ec8b3e99 / 8c1f0a87b / 9664b2e31 / 77d89d830 / c5f863136 all carry DESCRIPTION Version: 0.91.13 while their messages claim v0.92.0, v0.92.2, v0.92.3, v0.92.4, v0.92.5. column16: BEST RAW PSI IN THE PROGRAMME
column17: RAW-PSI MAE (burden-weighted, 6 selection blocks, no blending): D9b 0.1918, N5 0.1961, N8 0.1967, N6 0.1984, P000 0.1996, P000R 0.1998, P001 production 0.2022. D9b is -5.1% vs production and -3.9% vs P000, against a replicate noise of 0.1% (P000 0.1996 vs P000R 0.1998) -- about 39x the noise, so unambiguous. It also has the best WIS (0.1548 vs production 0.1653) and the best R2_sse (-5.751 vs -6.394). MEANING: forcing country differences to be a LINEAR MAP OF COUNTRY CHARACTERISTICS, with zero free parameters per country, beats a free learned ID embedding. That is the strongest evidence yet for the pool-by-similarity diagnosis, and it is a DATA change (covariates already sitting unused in the panel) rather than an architecture change. RANKING of the country-variability family by effect size vs P000: D9b -3.9% (39x noise), N5 -1.8% (18x), N8 -1.5% (15x), N6 -0.6% (6x, marginal). N6's sign-preservation constraint was therefore NOT the binding limitation.

column6: gamma_scale = 2, letting country modulation flip a trunk feature's sign
column7: tanh gamma is sign-preserving, so a covariate with opposite effects in two regimes must be averaged by the shared trunk
column16: MARGINAL -- SIGN PRESERVATION WAS NOT THE CONSTRAINT
column17: MAE 0.1984 vs P000 0.1996: -0.6%, about 6x the 0.1% replicate noise, so real but the smallest effect in the family. R2_corr 0.297 is BELOW P000's 0.301. The hypothesis was reasonable and is now answered: the inability to flip a feature's sign was not what limited the model.

column6: stack the blends on D9b's psi, which has the best RAW MAE of any arm
column7: a better psi should give a better blended product
column16: BETTER RAW PSI, WORSE BLEND -- AND THE REASON IS ACTIONABLE
column17: D9b + C12c_C11h is 0.1528 against N8 + C12c_C11h at 0.1511, and at weeks 9-13 D9b gives +4.9% vs persistence where N8 gives +5.7% -- so the arm with the BEST RAW psi (D9b 0.1918 vs N8 0.1967) produces the WORSE blend. EXPLANATION, and it follows from what each arm fixed: the blend takes its LEVEL from persistence and uses psi only for SHAPE, so only a shape improvement can transfer. D9b improved the level (best R2_sse -5.751) while N8 improved the shape (best R2_corr 0.321 vs D9b's 0.302), and the blend already had the level covered. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REST OF THE LADDER: judge a candidate psi for BLEND purposes on R2_corr, NOT on MAE. Ordering by raw R2_corr -- N8 0.321, N5 0.309, D9b 0.302, P000 0.301, N6 0.297 -- predicts the blend ordering already observed (N8 0.1602 > N5 0.1639 on C10_C11h). NOTE D9b + C12b gives 0.1502, the best OVERALL MAE measured, but overall MAE is dominated by weeks 1-4 where persistence is near-optimal by construction; on the 12-week horizon that actually matters, N8 still leads.
